"They do not classify every successful run" denies that every successful run falls under the sufficient conditions, i.e. some successful BFGS behavior satisfies none of them; the first clause only restates that the positive results are implications. This is the claim of energy.tex:311-311, covered in Lean by A/energy/prose/035 (certificate_not_necessary: an objective on which every admissible run converges while no sublevel admits band certificates; the radial, centered, homogeneous and polyhedral criteria all act through band certificates, and the planar criteria concern n=2). A/verification/prose/022.anchor: a branch change alone does not imply failure.
A/verification/prose/022.note: Stated as the non-implication it asserts: for every coercive finite maximum of linear functions, every infinite admissible run changes its active piece at every step (weak Wolfe gives y_k^Ts_k>0, so g_{k+1} differs from g_k) and still converges to the unique minimizer 0; such runs exist (fourMaxRun, for max{v,-v,3u+v/2,-3u+v/2}, built from the library run UnexcitedMetric.run). By contrast the seed G, a non-coercive maximum of three linear functions, has runs that change branch at every step and fail.
